sentences.text: The genus Jian contains only one species, Jian changmaensis, known from an articulated pectoral girdle and part of the forelimb, including the humerus, radius, and ulna.

It is considered a medium-sized microraptorine, larger than small Microraptor and Zhongjianosaurus but smaller than Sinornithosaurus and Changyuraptor, and the firm co-ossification of its scapula and coracoid indicates it belonged to a skeletally mature individual.

Unique features include a coracoid-to-humerus ratio greater than in any other microraptorine, distal humeral condyles primarily on the cranial surface, and a prominent foramen at the top of the radius in ventral view.
Fossil material of Jian was first reported in a conference abstract in 2010 after being discovered in 2008 near Changma village in northwest Gansu Province, China.

Ling-Qi Zhou and colleagues formally described Jian changmaensis as a new genus and species in 2026, designating specimen GSGM-D050 as the holotype, which is permanently housed in the Gansu Geological Museum.
Jian changmaensis is the first non-avian dinosaur described from the Xiagou Formation, following the discovery of over 100 bird fossils there.

Accumulations of shattered bird bones, similar to owl pellets, have been found at the Xiagou Formation site where Jian fossils occur, leading researchers to suggest that Jian may have produced these accumulations given it is the only non-bird there and one of the largest known microraptorines.
Jian is classified as a microraptorine dromaeosaurid, and phylogenetic analysis recovered it as a member of the dromaeosaurid subfamily Microraptorinae.
Phylogenetic analysis placed Jian in an unresolved polytomy with other derived microraptorines such as Hesperonychus, Microraptor, and Zhongjianosaurus.
Jian lived during the Early Cretaceous period, specifically the Aptian age, with a time range estimated to be between 121.4 and 113.2 million years ago.
The exact position of Jian within the Microraptorinae clade remains unresolved in current phylogenetic analyses.
